arxiv-2012-15087.title: Cooperation in a fluid swarm of fuel-free micro-swimmers
arxiv-2012-15087.creator: Matan Yah Ben Zion, Yaelin Caba, Alvin Modin, Paul M Chaikin
arxiv-2012-15087.description: Abstract Cooperation is vital for the survival of a swarm 1 . Large scale cooperation allows murmuring starlings to outmaneuver preying falcons 2 , shoaling sardines to outsmart sea lions 3 , and homosapiens to outlive their Pleistocene peers 4 .

arxiv-2104-04214.title: What is the ground truth? Reliability of multi-annotator data for audio tagging
arxiv-2104-04214.creator: Irene Martín-Morató, Annamaria Mesaros
arxiv-2104-04214.description: Abstract Crowdsourcing has become a common approach for annotating large amounts of data. It has the advantage of harnessing a large workforce to produce large amounts of data in a short time, but comes with the disadvantage of employing non-expert annotators with different backgrounds.

arxiv-2111-12691.title: On the variational principle in the unfolded dynamics
arxiv-2111-12691.creator: A.A. Tarusov
arxiv-2111-12691.description: Abstract The interplay between off-shell and on-shell unfolded systems is analyzed. The formulation of invariant constraints that put an off-shell system on shell is developed by adding new variables and derivation in the target space, that extends the original Q Q -derivation of the unfolded system to a bicomplex.

arxiv-2301-10919.title: Joint action loss for proximal policy optimization
arxiv-2301-10919.creator: Xiulei Song, Yizhao Jin, & Greg Slabaugh & Simon Lucas
arxiv-2301-10919.description: Abstract PPO (Proximal Policy Optimization) is a state-of-the-art policy gradient algorithm that has been successfully applied to complex computer games such as Dota 2 and Honor of Kings. In these environments, an agent makes compound actions consisting of multiple sub-actions. PPO uses clipping to restrict policy updates.

arxiv-2303-16645.creator: A.S. Gorban , 1 , 2 ,^{1,2} S.V. Molkov , 1 ,^{1} A.A. Lutovinov , 1 ,^{1} A.N. Semena , 1 ,^{1} 1 Space Research Institute of the Russian Academy of Sciences, Profsoyuznaya 84/32, 117997 Moscow, Russia 2 Higher School of Economics, Myasnitskaya 20, 101000 Moscow, Russia
arxiv-2303-16645.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by A.S. Gorban , 1 , 2 ,^{1,2} S.V. Molkov , 1 ,^{1} A.A. Lutovinov , 1 ,^{1} A.N. Semena , 1 ,^{1} 1 Space Research Institute of the Russian Academy of Sciences, Profsoyuznaya 84/32, 117997 Moscow, Russia 2 Higher School of Economics, Myasnitskaya 20, 101000 Moscow, Russia. arxiv-2404-04505.title: Exploring UAV Networking from the Terrain Information Completeness Perspective: A Tutorial Thanks: Zhengying Lou, Ruibo Wang, Baha Eddine Youcef Belmekki and Mohamed-Slim Alouini are with King Abdullah University of Science and Technology (KAUST), CEMSE division, Thuwal 23955-6900, Saudi Arabia. Mus
arxiv-2404-04505.creator: Zhengying Lou, Ruibo Wang
arxiv-2404-04505.description: Abstract Terrain information is a crucial factor affecting the performance of unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) networks. As a tutorial, this article provides a unique perspective on the completeness of terrain information, summarizing and enhancing the research on terrain-based UAV deployment.

arxiv-2410-16822.title: Can Large Language Models Act as Ensembler for Multi-GNNs?
arxiv-2410-16822.creator: Hanqi Duan, Yao Cheng, Jianxiang Yu, Yao Liu, Xiang Li
arxiv-2410-16822.description: Abstract Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) have emerged as powerful models for learning from graph-structured data. However, GNNs lack the inherent semantic understanding capability of rich textual node attributes, limiting their effectiveness in applications. On the other hand, we empirically observe that for existing GNN models, no one can consistently outperforms others across diverse datasets.

arxiv-2503-01067.title: All Roads Lead to Likelihood: The Value of Reinforcement Learning in Fine-Tuning
arxiv-2503-01067.creator: Gokul Swamy, Sanjiban Choudhury & Wen Sun, Zhiwei Steven Wu & J. Andrew Bagnell
arxiv-2503-01067.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Gokul Swamy, Sanjiban Choudhury & Wen Sun, Zhiwei Steven Wu & J. Andrew Bagnell. From a first-principles perspective, it may seem odd that the strongest results in foundation model fine-tuning (FT) are achieved via a relatively complex, two-stage training procedure.

arxiv-2509-16784.title: Controlled Yet Natural: A Hybrid BDI-LLM Conversational Agent for Child Helpline Training Conference: Preprint version. Accepted at IVA ’25; Preprint version. Accepted at IVA ’25; CCS: Applied computing Interactive learning environments CCS: Human-centered computing Empirical studies in HCI CCS: Com
arxiv-2509-16784.creator: Mohammed Al Owayyed, Adarsh Denga, Willem-Paul Brinkman
arxiv-2509-16784.description: Abstract . Child helpline training often relies on human-led roleplay, which is both time- and resource-consuming. To address this, rule-based interactive agent simulations have been proposed to provide a structured training experience for new counsellors. However, these agents might suffer from limited language understanding and response variety.

arxiv-2510-06273.title: Vision Transformer for Transient Noise Classification
arxiv-2510-06273.creator: D. Srivastava, A. Niedzielski, [4pt] Institute of Astronomy, Nicolaus Copernicus University in Toruń ul. Gagarina 11, 87-100 Toruń, Poland
arxiv-2510-06273.description: Abstract Transient noise (glitches) in LIGO data hinders the detection of gravitational waves (GW). The Gravity Spy project has categorised these noise events into various classes. With the O3 run, there is the inclusion of two additional noise classes and thus a need to train new models for effective classification.

arxiv-2510-18216.title: Representations of the Drinfeld doubles of pointed rank one Hopf algebras Thanks: 2010 Mathematics Subject Classification . 16T99, 16E99, 16G70
arxiv-2510-18216.creator: Hua Sun, Hui-Xiang Chen, Yinhuo Zhang
arxiv-2510-18216.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Hua Sun, Hui-Xiang Chen, Yinhuo Zhang. In this paper, we investigate the representations of the Drinfeld doubles D ⁡ ( H 𝒟 ) D(H_{\mathcal{D}}) of pointed rank one Hopf algebras H 𝒟 H_{\mathcal{D}} over an algebraically closed field 𝕜 \Bbbk of characteristic zero. We provide a complete classification of all finite-dimensional indecomposable D ⁡ ( H 𝒟 ) D(H_{\mathcal{D}}) -modules up to isomorphism and explicitly describe the Auslander-Reiten sequences in the category of finite-dimensional D ⁡ ( H 𝒟 ) D(H_{\mathcal{D}}) -modules.

arxiv-2510-25951.title: Estimating cognitive biases with attention-aware inverse planning
arxiv-2510-25951.creator: Sounak Banerjee, Daphne Cornelisse, Deepak Gopinath, Emily Sumner, Jonathan DeCastro, Guy Rosman, Eugene Vinitsky, Mark K. Ho
arxiv-2510-25951.description: Abstract People’s goal-directed behaviors are influenced by their cognitive biases, and autonomous systems that interact with people should be aware of this. For example, people’s attention to objects in their environment will be biased in a way that systematically affects how they perform everyday tasks such as driving to work.

arxiv-2512-24226.title: Rarita-Schwinger model in Very Special Relativity
arxiv-2512-24226.creator: M. C. Araújo, J. Furtado, J. G. Lima, T. Mariz
arxiv-2512-24226.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by M. C. Araújo, J. Furtado, J. G. Lima, T. Mariz. In this work, we investigate vacuum polarization in the Rarita-Schwinger model within the framework of Very Special Relativity. We examine both massive and massless spin- 3 / 2 3/2 fields coupled to the Maxwell field. The Mandelstam-Leibbrandt prescription is applied in order to evaluate the one-loop integrals, and we work within the S ​ I ​ M ​ ( 2 ) SIM(2) limit.

pmc-11353871.title: The Perception and Roles of School Mental Health Professionals Regarding School Bullying (Suluk Audwani) in Oman: A Qualitative Study in an Urban Setting
pmc-11353871.creator: Muna Al Saadoon, Rawaa Abubakr Abuelgassim Eltayib, Amjad Hassan Alhaj, Moon Fai Chan, Said Aldhafri, Samir Al-Adawi
pmc-11353871.description: With increasing mental health risks among school populations and prevalent bullying, school mental health professionals (SMHP) are crucial globally. This study explores the perspectives of SMHP on bullying in Omani schools, focussing on definitions, types, current practices, and future strategies.

pmc-11625235.title: Protocol for reticulocyte enrichment from low-volume human blood samples from alpha-thalassemic and healthy participants
pmc-11625235.creator: Stefano Comità, Paola Valentino, Teresa Ceglie, Neha Kargutkar, Harish Kalaiarasan, Giovanni Battista Ferrero, Antonella Roetto
pmc-11625235.description: SummaryReticulocyte isolation from peripheral blood is crucial for hematological research. Here, we present a protocol for high-quality reticulocyte enrichment from small blood quantities obtained from alpha-thalassemic and healthy participants. We describe steps for Ficoll and Percoll gradient centrifugation to obtain a reticulocyte-enriched fraction, followed by negative immunomagnetic separation to remove granulocytes and platelets.

pmc-11690741.title: A LOOK AT STUDENT CAREGIVING EXPERIENCES: OPPORTUNITIES FOR CAMPUSES AND COMMUNITIES
pmc-11690741.creator: Allyson Graf, Katherina Nikzad-Terhune, Joseph Gaugler
pmc-11690741.description: Caregiving in the United States continues to be a significant and growing phenomenon that warrants ongoing exploration of ways to support caregivers. Further examining the impact that intergenerational connections and age-inclusive practices have on the caregiving experience can help inform ways for both campuses and communities to be more responsive to caregiver needs.

pmc-11895869.title: Neferine inhibits the development of lung cancer cells by downregulating TGF‐β to regulate MST1/ROS‐induced pyroptosis
pmc-11895869.creator: Peng‐Cheng Zhong, Zhi‐Wen Liu, Qi‐Chang Xing, Jia Chen, Rui‐Pei Yang
pmc-11895869.description: Non‐small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) accounts for ~85% of all lung cancer cases. Neferine is used as a traditional Chinese medicine with many pharmacological effects, including antitumor properties; however, it has not been reported whether neferine plays an anticancer role by causing pyroptosis in NSCLC cells.

pmc-12437008.title: Early detection of pediatric bipolar disorders: a systematic review and meta-analysis
pmc-12437008.creator: C. Alcaino
pmc-12437008.description: IntroductionBipolar disorders (BD) are among the most impairing of pediatric psychiatric disorders. Even though BD symptoms may begin in adolescence, they are frequently not diagnosed until adulthood. BD screening tests could aid diagnostic assessment in paediatric populations and are supported by The International Society for Paediatric Bipolar Disorders Task Force and empirical evidence.

pmc-12455798.title: Conventional probe trabeculotomy versus microcatheter-assisted 360° trabeculotomy (PIRATE) in childhood glaucoma—study protocol for a randomized controlled trial
pmc-12455798.creator: Julia V. Stingl, Irene M. Schmidtmann, Markus Schepers, Alexander K. Schuster, Jasmin Rezapour, Anna M. Welzel, Angi L. Mendoza-Moreira, Heike Elflein, Anne Ehrlich, Claudia Wolf, Michael Hopp, Ingeborg Stalmans, Sophie Lemmens, Thomas Dietlein, Silvia Schrittenlocher, Alexandra Lappas, Claudia Schu
pmc-12455798.description: BackgroundTo compare the success and safety of microcatheter-assisted 360° trabeculotomy (MCAT) with conventional probe trabeculotomy in a large, heterogeneous cohort of children with primary or secondary glaucoma.MethodsIn this prospective, multicenter, observer-blinded, randomized controlled trial, 76 children (152 eyes) with bilateral primary or secondary childhood glaucoma aged ≤ 12 years will be included.

pmc-12604314.title: Association between cardiac radiation dose and coronary artery calcification progression in breast cancer patients after radiotherapy: the modifying role of concomitant systemic inflammation (BACCARAT study)
pmc-12604314.creator: Médéa Locquet, Georges Tarlet, David Broggio, Gaëlle Jimenez, Jérémy Camilleri, Matthieu Lapeyre, Jean Ferrières, Fabien Milliat, Sophie Jacob
pmc-12604314.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Radiation-induced cardiotoxicity remains a significant concern in breast cancer (BC) patients treated with radiotherapy (RT), with both cardiac radiation exposure and systemic inflammation emerging as key contributors to early cardiovascular complications. This study investigated whether cardiac radiation dose triggers independently or synergistically with systemic inflammation, characterized by C-reactive protein (CRP) elevation to predict coronary artery calcification (CAC) progression in BC survivors.

pmc-13125063.title: Neurosurgery to restore function in cerebral palsy: current practice and emerging therapies
pmc-13125063.creator: Akshay Sankar, Awa Jobe, Bailey McDonald, Taylor J. Abel, Amit Sinha, Martin G. Piazza
pmc-13125063.description: Cerebral palsy (CP) affects 1.5–2.5 per 1,000 live births and manifests as diverse movement disorders including spasticity, dystonia, and mixed phenotypes that significantly impact motor function and quality of life. This review examines surgical and neuromodulatory interventions for medically refractory CP-associated movement disorders.

pmc-13215168.title: Active protein-capturing hydrogel for broad-spectrum pathogen defense
pmc-13215168.creator: Jiaming Liu, Shiqi Hu, Mengrui Liu, Savannah Weihang Zhang, Na Yan, Xuan Mei, Dashuai Zhu, Ming Shen, Ke Cheng
pmc-13215168.description: Proteinaceous agents, including viral particles and allergenic proteins, play central roles in infection, inflammation, and immune dysregulation, yet few materials can broadly neutralize them through direct protein capture. Here, we present an inhalable protein trap (IPT), an active hydrogel that rapidly immobilizes diverse amine-containing biomolecules via NHS-amine chemistry.

pmc-13233245.title: Conservative management without routine bailout stent for non-flow-limiting dissection after DCB angioplasty: a prospective three-arm study
pmc-13233245.creator: Jie Chen, Dewen Zhu, Hailiang Ma, Yuanben Lu, Zhenhua Jiang
pmc-13233245.description: The optimal management of non-flow-limiting coronary dissection after drug-coated balloon (DCB) angioplasty remains controversial, particularly in Asian populations. We conducted a prospective, three-arm cohort study to evaluate whether conservative management of non-flow-limiting dissection is non-inferior to bailout stent in patients with de novo medium-to-large coronary artery lesions.

pmc-13323878.title: Panax ginseng as a microbial ecosystem modulator: implications for systemic health via the gut-organ axes
pmc-13323878.creator: Xiang Li, Yuyang Zhao, Ning Liu, Yixin Zhang, Ruoyan Liu, Wenhui Shan, Jie Zhang, Tianli Chen
pmc-13323878.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Meyer, a renowned medicinal herb, exerts many of its systemic effects through intricate interactions with the gut microbiota, a relationship that also addresses the challenge of its own limited oral bioavailability. This review comprehensively examines the role of ginseng and its bioactive constituents in modulating gut microbiota and their subsequent influence on host health through key gut-organ axes.

pmc-13407165.title: Radical climate protests shaped portrayals of moderate activists and reader attitudes in German news media
pmc-13407165.creator: Lukas Mayrhofer, Simon Fassnacht, Markus Foramitti, Jana K Köhler, Boryana Todorova, Claus Lamm, Mauricio Martins

pmc-13525070.title: Substrate type and termite discovery shape decomposition at the dry end of an African savanna rainfall gradient
pmc-13525070.creator: Katherine Bunney, Mark Robertson, Paul Eggleton, Sally Archibald, Catherine Parr
pmc-13525070.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Decomposition is the process by which dead plant biomass is recycled and made available again for uptake by other plants. It is largely mediated by microbes and soil invertebrates. Global decomposition studies have demonstrated that decomposition is primarily temperature-driven with rainfall playing a secondary role, although to date, all global decomposition studies have used a single substrate to measure decomposition meaning differences with substrate type may be missed.

pmc-13584826.title: Motivational and emotional determinants of health goal progress in inflammatory bowel disease: a longitudinal study
pmc-13584826.creator: Barbara Horvát, Anett Dávid, Viola Sallay, Beatrix Rafael, Sanela Njers, Kata Orbán, Tamás Molnár, Márta Csabai, Ádám Tóth, Tamás Martos
pmc-13584826.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundSelf-management among patients with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) is influenced by motivational and emotional factors. Although research has increasingly highlighted psychological support, it has underexplored interactions among goal-related emotions, motivation types, and progress in health-related behavior.MethodsA total of 123 adults diagnosed with IBD participated in a longitudinal study, completing questionnaires at baseline (T1) and at follow-ups after three months (T2) and six months (T3). Measures included self-concordance (autonomous and controlled motivation), positive and negative emotions, and goal progress.
